title: Re-issue of 20261025T0950-c09-review-pcell-contained (same seed-9 labkit run and verdict; the seed result text was misread as a failed replication)
summary: Fresh seed 9. contain.py to t=20000: every cell holds its particles at >= 86x the 2-6 px shell (median: empty shell), 93% of particles inside cells, as claimed. labkit T=100000: cells from an unstructured start, 15 persistent splits to generation 3 (merges 2); c06's genealogy on the same seed: 25 splits, 56 deaths, 0 merges, 0 flips. Selection at the last snapshot replicates (35/37 mature deaths below the median, mean percentile 0.07; marker 0.50; splits 0.66; parent-daughter r 0.86). Two problems: (1) bodies are not bounded: on seed 9 one cell grows to 42% of all particles in cells by t=40000, breaks up, then regrows to 77% (9741 particles against a median of 136) at t=100000 (rerun/seed9/particles.png, largest_cell_s9.txt); claim seed 2 reaches 53%. (2) As in my multilevel review, the dying cells are at yield percentile 0.48 at birth (splitting cells 0.63); their low yield accumulates during life. Weak.

observations.S: rerun/seed9/particles.png t=0: uniform particle soup over the whole domain; ~20 cells by t=4500
observations.I: rerun/seed9/particles.png t=4500-52000: discrete cells of bounded size; but from t=56500 one cell grows without dividing to 77% of all particles in cells at t=100000 (largest_cell_s9.txt)
observations.W: W/c_world_s9.log: min per-cell ratio 86-290x at every check t=1000-20000, 100% of cells >= 2x, 93% of particles inside cells
observations.D: rerun/seed9/lineage.png: 15 persistent splits, max generation 3, 2 merges; data/selection_s9.txt genealogy: 25 splits, 0 merges
observations.H: data/selection_s9.txt: 35/37 mature deaths below the living median (mean percentile 0.071), inert marker 0.50, splits 0.66, parent-daughter r 0.86; at birth the dying cells are at 0.48 and splitting cells at 0.63 (lifesel.py)

seeds_run.result: pass for S, W, D and the last-snapshot H differential; one cell grows unbounded after t~56000 (I weak late); birth-time H weak

controls_run.W: none of my own beyond the fresh-seed containment readout (the gate-off and lowered-D controls are the author's)
controls_run.H: the claim's inert marker on seed 9, and the lifesel.py birth/mid/late readout

verdicts.limitation: Containment is the reflection rule itself (a particle step to lower phi is accepted with probability (phi_new/phi_old)^2), so W holds by construction; the author says so. Individuals are not bounded on every seed: one cell can grow to hold most of the population (77% on seed 9, 53% on claim seed 2), which also distorts the yield percentiles late in the run. The death differential is mostly acquired during life (dying cells at percentile 0.48 at birth on seed 9; 0.36-0.55 on the claim's seeds), so inheritance predicts fate only modestly. One fresh seed.
